title: ÆTHER: Kingdom (main title theme of the movie)
story: The film's main theme: the hero, the land he protects and the people who believe in him. It plays over the title card and returns at the hero's biggest moments.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 07:49: one or two hero entry BGMs, 'a proper cinematic main BGM of the movie', made without his input. Track 2 is the title theme, built to sit beside Storm Entry but contrast it: slower heavy stomp (refs R4-R6, 88 BPM) that switches into a tisram 6/8 swing, Kiravani-style minor raga (a big singable melody, rule 14), heroic and emotional rather than menacing. Same rules: mystery start with one sound plus a grab in 3 s, motif at both ends, one reversed veena swell, new hook every 8-12 s, a composed interlude showpiece (flute and violin counterpoint, natural and dry), counter-melody and moving melodic bass, one-beat silence and slam, whole-step key lift with a hundred-voice wordless choir, korvai ending. Prompt mode (music_v2).

prompt: A brand-new MAIN TITLE THEME of a big South Indian action film, the hero's theme that plays over the title card: majestic, heroic and emotional, it makes the whole theatre stand up. Written the way the greatest Tamil and Telugu film composers write a blockbuster main theme: a big singable melody, not a loop. About 88 BPM, a heavy, proud stomp felt in half-time, in a minor raga like Kiravani (harmonic minor, a sad-proud colour), modal harmony over a deep pedal bass with one borrowed major chord at the climax. INDIAN TOUCH IN THE WRITING: the melody is phrased like a playback singer, question-and-answer phrases with fast gamakam slides, grace notes and long bent held notes on every lead; the Tamil mass bounce; a switch into a swinging triplet 6/8 (tisram) feel in the middle; tight unison band stabs; the hook coming back bigger each time; a korvai-style ending. Balance: real instruments (a bamboo flute, solo violin and a violin section, cello, French horns and low brass, mridangam, thavil, big taiko-like drums) carry half the music, played close, natural and dry like real musicians, no echo on the flute or violin; the other half is fresh electronics: a deep warm synth bass, a soaring gritty synth lead, and processed Carnatic sounds: a stuttering glitch-chopped veena riff and a mridangam pitched down into the deep bass hit. Wordless voices, no lyrics: one deep male voice humming the theme, a male crowd chant, and later a huge choir. Timeline: 0-3 s: one deep, bent synth note with a massive cinematic low boom, then a lone solo violin plays a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, last note bent upward) with a slide. 3-10 s: mystery: only the violin and a deep drone; a lone deep male voice hums the first phrase of the theme; one slow mridangam pulse. 10-12 s: one reversed veena swell into a huge full-band hit. 12-24 s: the proud stomp begins: heavy drums, deep synth bass, the main theme on French horns and the synth lead in unison, the chopped veena answering each phrase, a crowd chant on the accents. 24-34 s: the theme moves to the violin section in Indian-style unison with fast runs, the cello plays a melodic bass line like a second melody, the brass answers. 34-46 s: surprise: the groove switches into a swinging triplet 6/8 feel, thavil and mridangam leading; the interlude showpiece: the bamboo flute and the solo violin play a fast virtuoso counterpoint, chasing and answering each other, natural and dry. 46-47 s: one beat of total silence. 47-60 s: SLAM: a hundred-voice wordless choir sings the main theme a whole step higher, full drums back in the heavy stomp, brass and strings at full power, the synth lead soaring above with bends, the biggest moment of the track. 60-72 s: the theme one last time in its grandest form, the borrowed major chord lifting it into triumph, the crowd chant answering, a thavil roll building. 72-80 s: the ending: a rhythmic korvai phrase played three times by the whole band, landing on one massive final chord with a sub drop, then the solo violin plays the 3-note call once more and the last note bends and rings. Clean, warm, wide, glossy, very loud cinematic mix with a deep sub. Not Western trailer music, not Hollywood epic, not EDM, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no filter sweeps, no long quiet stretches, no wall of synths, no lyrics.
